lessons: When an enemy army threatens our capital or critical supply hubs, use move or rail to concentrate our forces for defense rather than continuing routine drills.
When an idle army is in a secure city with recruitment available, use recruit to expand our military strength rather than only drilling.
When an army is adjacent to an enemy city with inferior numbers or unfavorable odds, do not move or attack; instead, drill or fortify until superior strength or supply is secured.
When a naval fleet is built, use fleet sail to clear or blockade enemy ports rather than engaging in unguided raids.
When a new army is raised with recruit, let it rest and do not order it to move on the same turn.
When an army has supply 1 or less, use supply <army> immediately before moving or ending the turn.
